plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 after iteration_10 material_data failure with 0 valid candidates. Three routes proposed: (1) MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack with enforced minimum thickness bounds (≥20 nm) and quarter-wave initialization centered on passband to prevent TMM phase singularities; (2) SiO2/HfO2 periodic photonic crystal with AR matching layers based on evidence from CorpusId:199509322; (3) Reduced 16-layer MgF2/HfO2 stack with wider thickness search bounds to improve optimizer convergence. All routes preserve the 30-layer maximum, no-metal constraint, and three-band spectral objectives.

routes.title: MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack with enforced minimum thickness and quarter-wave initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The iteration_10 failure arose from thickness values approaching zero or negative values during optimization, triggering TMM phase singularities. Enforcing explicit minimum thickness bounds (≥20 nm) and initializing from quarter-wave optical depths centered on the 267.5 nm passband midpoint will produce physically valid candidates while maintaining the chirped dispersion strategy that achieved 0.647 target score in iteration_06.
routes.design_principle: Alternating high/low index layers with thicknesses varying gradually across the stack to create broadband rejection outside the passband while maintaining constructive interference in the 255-280 nm transmission band.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
Quarter-wave optical thickness principle for bandpass filter design
expected_advantages: Enforced minimum bounds prevent TMM numerical failures
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Chirped dispersion maintains broadband rejection capability from iteration_06
known_risks: May still converge to local optima if search budget insufficient
MgF2 refractive index dispersion in deep UV may differ from nominal values
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2 (20 finite layers total). Each layer thickness bounded between 20 nm and 200 nm. Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical depth centered on 267.5 nm wavelength (MgF2 n≈1.38, HfO2 n≈2.0 at UV). Use coherent S-matrix solver across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Score three transmittance objectives: maximize mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use bound-aware global optimizer with projection of out-of-bounds samples back into feasible region. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration_10 failed with 0 valid candidates due to material_data error. This route enforces explicit minimum thickness bounds (≥20 nm) to prevent TMM phase singularities, widens thickness search interval centered on quarter-wave values, and switches to bound-aware global optimizer with projection as directed in feedback.

routes.title: SiO2/HfO2 periodic photonic crystal with AR matching layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Based on evidence from CorpusId:199509322, a periodic (L/2 H L/2)m photonic crystal structure with anti-reflection matching layers can achieve high transmissivity in a narrow UV passband while providing strong stopband rejection. SiO2/HfO2 material pair offers better UV transparency than MgF2 in some deposition conditions and higher index contrast for stronger rejection.
routes.design_principle: Periodic main-function units (L/2 H L/2) sandwiched between two anti-reflection coatings, optimized using Transfer Matrix Method with experimental optical constants.
routes.proposed_topology: 18-layer stack: Air | SiO2(AR) | HfO2(AR) | SiO2(AR) | SiO2(L/2) | HfO2(H) | SiO2(L/2) | SiO2(L/2) | HfO2(H) | SiO2(L/2) | SiO2(L/2) | HfO2(H) | SiO2(L/2) | SiO2(L/2) | HfO2(H) | SiO2(L/2) | SiO2(AR) | HfO2(AR) | SiO2(AR) | fused silica
manufacturing_considerations: minimum thickness 15 nm for AR layers
SiO2 and HfO2 are conventional depositable dielectrics
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method optimization with experimental optical constants
expected_advantages: Periodic structure provides predictable stopband position and width
AR matching layers reduce passband reflection losses
SiO2/HfO2 pair has demonstrated UV filter performance in literature
known_risks: Periodic structure may have narrower passband than chirped design
SiO2 absorption edge near 200 nm may affect 255 nm transmission
Requires precise thickness control to maintain periodicity
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize an 18-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (18 finite layers total). First 3 and last 3 layers serve as anti-reflection matching; middle 12 layers form 4-period (L/2 H L/2) photonic crystal units. Each layer thickness bounded between 15 nm and 150 nm. Initialize AR layers at 25 nm, periodic L layers at 30 nm, periodic H layers at 45 nm. Use coherent S-matrix solver across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Score three transmittance objectives: maximize mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use differential evolution optimizer with 100 population members. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Alternative topology to chirped stack based on literature evidence for periodic photonic crystal UV filters. Different material pair (SiO2/HfO2 vs MgF2/HfO2) tests whether material_data failure in iteration_10 was material-specific. Provides complementary design family to validate scientific principle.

routes.title: Reduced 16-layer MgF2/HfO2 stack with expanded thickness search bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 20 to 16 decreases optimization dimensionality, improving convergence reliability. Expanding thickness bounds (15-250 nm) allows optimizer to explore thicker layers that may provide better broadband rejection. This tests whether iteration_10 failure was due to optimization complexity rather than material data issues.
routes.design_principle: Simplified alternating high/low index stack with fewer layers but wider individual thickness ranges to maintain spectral performance with reduced optimization complexity.
routes.proposed_topology: 16-layer alternating stack: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Fewer optimization variables improves convergence reliability
Wider thickness bounds allow exploration of thicker quarter-wave stacks for IR rejection
Same material pair as successful iteration_06 maintains continuity
known_risks: Fewer layers may reduce stopband rejection depth
Wider bounds may increase search space and require more optimization iterations
May not achieve same performance as 20-layer designs
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2 (16 finite layers total). Each layer thickness bounded between 15 nm and 250 nm. Initialize all thicknesses at 80 nm (uniform starting point). Use coherent S-matrix solver across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Score three transmittance objectives: maximize mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use CMA-ES optimizer with 50 population members and 200 generation budget. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether iteration_10 failure was optimization complexity related rather than material-specific. Reduced dimensionality (16 vs 20 variables) with expanded bounds provides complementary search strategy. If this succeeds where iteration_10 failed, suggests bound/initialization issues rather than material data problems.

research_influence: Evidence from CorpusId:199509322 motivated route_02_refine_02 periodic photonic crystal topology with (L/2 H L/2)m units and AR matching layers
Evidence from CorpusId:211025653 on HfO2/SiO2 material properties and deposition methods informed material choices in all three routes
Evidence from CorpusId:16516444 on ALD precision and thickness control supported the hypothesis that explicit thickness bounds prevent numerical failures
Iteration_06 success with 0.647 target score using MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack validated this material pair for route_02_refine_01 and route_02_refine_03
Iteration_10 failure with 0 valid candidates drove the enforcement of minimum thickness bounds and bound-aware optimizer selection
unresolved_decisions: Whether MgF2 or SiO2 provides better UV transparency at 255 nm in actual deposition conditions
Whether periodic or chirped topology better balances passband transmission with dual stopband rejection
Whether 16, 18, or 20 layers provides optimal tradeoff between performance and optimization convergence
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
